citation.title: Conservative Variance Estimation for Sampling Designs with Zero Pairwise Inclusion Probabilities

standing_assumptions:
The work is a short theory paper (Survey Methodology, June 2013, Vol. 39, No. 1, printed pp. 231–241; the article is PDF pp. 3–13 of the staged main.pdf) with two propositions and three corollaries, each with a printed proof, and an official simulation supplement (staged/supplements/smj_suppl.pdf, printed pp. A1–A10) that the article points to on p. 239. Everything below was read from the rendered page images (the staged pages, and the staged PDFs re-rendered at 220 dpi when this list was fixed).
[Population and design: Section 2, first paragraph, pp. 232–233 (PDF pp. 4–5)] “Consider a population $U$ indexed by $1, \ldots, k, \ldots N$ and a sampling design such that the probability of inclusion in the sample for unit $k$ is $\pi_k$, and the joint inclusion probability for units $k$ and $l$ is $\pi_{kl}$. Under a measurable design, there are two conditions: (1) $\pi_k > 0$ and $\pi_k$ is known for all $k \in U$ and (2) $\pi_{kl} > 0$ and $\pi_{kl}$ is known for all $k, l \in U$. Non-measurable designs include those for which either of the two conditions for a measurable design do not hold. Failure to meet the former condition precludes unbiased estimation of totals.”
[Estimator of the total and inclusion indicators: p. 233 (PDF p. 5)] “The Horvitz-Thompson estimator of a population total is $\hat t = \sum_{k \in s} y_k/\pi_k = \sum_{k \in U} I_k\, y_k/\pi_k$, where $I_k \in \{0, 1\}$ is unit $k$'s inclusion indicator, the only stochastic component of the expression, with $\mathrm{E}(I_k) = \pi_k$, the inclusion probability, and $s$ and $U$ refer to the sample and the population, respectively. Define $\mathrm{E}(I_k I_l) = \pi_{kl}$, which is the probability that both units $k$ and $l$ from $U$ are included in the sample. Since $I_k I_k = I_k$, $\mathrm{E}(I_k I_k) = \pi_{kk} = \pi_k$ by construction. When condition 1 holds, as we assume throughout, the Horvitz-Thompson estimator is unbiased.”
[Variance and its estimator under measurability: Section 2.1, p. 233 (PDF p. 5)] “By Horvitz and Thompson (1952), the variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator for the total is $$\mathrm{Var}(\hat t) = \sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in U}\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l)\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l} = \sum_{k \in U}\mathrm{Var}(I_k)\left(\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\right)^2 + \sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in U\backslash k}\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l)\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l}.$$ We label a sample from a measurable design, $s^M$, and an unbiased estimator for $\mathrm{Var}(\hat t)$ on $s^M$ is $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t) = \sum_{k \in s^M}\sum_{l \in s^M}\frac{\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l)}{\pi_{kl}}\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l} = \sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in U} I_k I_l\frac{\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l)}{\pi_{kl}}\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l},$$ where the only stochastic part of the expression is $I_k I_l$, and unbiasedness is by $\mathrm{E}(I_k I_l) = \pi_{kl}$.”
[Non-measurable designs, the term $A$ and the sample $s^0$: Section 2.2, pp. 233–234 (PDF pp. 5–6)] “We now examine the case where condition 2 does not hold: $\pi_{kl} = 0$ for some units $k, l \in U$. Because $I_k$ is a Bernoulli random variable with probability $\pi_k$, $\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l) = \pi_{kl} - \pi_k\pi_l$ for $k \ne l$, and $\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_k) = \mathrm{Var}(I_k) = \pi_k(1 - \pi_k)$. Then, we can re-express the variance above as, $$\mathrm{Var}(\hat t) = \sum_{k \in U}\pi_k(1 - \pi_k)\left(\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\right)^2 + \sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in U\backslash k}(\pi_{kl} - \pi_k\pi_l)\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l}$$ $$= \sum_{k \in U}\pi_k(1 - \pi_k)\left(\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\right)^2 + \sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in \{U\backslash k:\pi_{kl} > 0\}}(\pi_{kl} - \pi_k\pi_l)\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l} - \underbrace{\sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in \{U\backslash k:\pi_{kl} = 0\}} y_k y_l}_{A}.$$ For $k$ and $l$ such that $\pi_{kl} = 0$, the sampling design will never permit unbiased estimation of the component of the variance labeled as $A$ above, since we will never observe $y_k$ and $y_l$ together. We label a sample from a design where condition 2 fails as $s^0$. When $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ is applied to $s^0$, the result is unbiased for $\mathrm{Var}(\hat t) + A$.” On the page the underbrace spans the double sum $\sum_k\sum_l y_k y_l$ only, not the minus sign before it, so $A = \sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in \{U\backslash k:\pi_{kl} = 0\}} y_k y_l$; Proposition 1 (p. 234) and the display of $A$ at the head of p. 239 (PDF p. 11) agree with this.
[Conventions that every statement inherits] The outcomes $y_1, \ldots, y_N$ are fixed real numbers; expectation, variance and covariance are over the sampling design alone (‘the only stochastic component’ is $I_k$). Condition 1 ($\pi_k > 0$ for every $k$) is assumed throughout; ‘known’ plays no part in any mathematical statement. A double sum $\sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in \{U\backslash k:\pi_{kl} = 0\}}$ runs over ordered pairs $(k, l)$ of distinct units with $\pi_{kl} = 0$, so each unordered pair is counted twice; $\sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in \{U:\pi_{kl} > 0\}}$ includes the diagonal $l = k$ (as $\pi_{kk} = \pi_k > 0$). On a sample $s^0$ the estimator $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ is the sum over pairs of sampled units, which the proof of Proposition 1 (p. 234) writes as $\sum_{k \in U}\sum_{l \in \{U:\pi_{kl} > 0\}} I_k I_l\frac{\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l)}{\pi_{kl}}\frac{y_k}{\pi_k}\frac{y_l}{\pi_l}$.
[What the paper does not print] No probability space is displayed: a sampling design is a probability distribution on the subsets $s \subseteq U$, with $I_k = 1$ exactly when $k \in s$. The paper does not say that $U$ is finite and non-empty other than through the indexing $1, \ldots, N$. In Section 3 the exponents $a_{kl}, b_{kl}$ are indexed by ordered pairs and are not required to be symmetric in $(k, l)$; $1/a_{kl} + 1/b_{kl} = 1$ with both positive forces $a_{kl}, b_{kl} > 1$; $|y|^{a}$ is the real power of a nonnegative number (so $|0|^{a} = 0$).
[Supplement, Section A, p. A1 (supplement PDF p. 1)] “In the simulations, expected values of $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ and $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\hat t)$ were computed exactly using expressions from Propositions 1 and 2 in the main text. Expected values for alternative estimators were computed using exact expressions for bias when available and via simulated sample draws otherwise. All simulations study expected values of estimators for the sampling variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator for the population mean, $$\hat\mu_{HT} \equiv \frac{1}{N}\hat t.$$” So in the supplement the estimand is $\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = \mathrm{Var}(\hat t)/N^2$ and the estimators are $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ and $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$; by Proposition 1 the bias of $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ is $A/N^2$.
[Supplement, Section B, one unit per stratum: pp. A1–A2 (supplement PDF pp. 1–2)] “Simplifying that context, we consider two strata each of size $M$, in which case $N = 2M$. From each stratum a single unit is randomly sampled. Thus, for unit $k$ in stratum $s$, $$\pi_{ks} = \pi = \frac{1}{M},$$ and for units $k$ and $l$ in strata 1 or 2, we have $$\pi_{ks,lt} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } s = t \\ \frac{1}{M^2} & \text{if } s \neq t \end{cases}.$$ In stratum $s$, outcomes $y_s = (y_{1s}, ..., y_{Ms})$ are drawn as, $$y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{is},$$ where $\alpha_s$ is a stratum-specific constant and $\epsilon_{ks} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, 1)$. For the two strata, 1 and 2, we keep things simple by setting $\alpha_1 = \alpha = -\alpha_2$, in which case the intra-class correlation over strata is given by, $$\rho_{ICC} = \frac{\alpha^2}{\alpha^2 + 1/2}.$$ We simulated 1,000 sets of outcomes, $(y_1, y_2)$ over varying values of $M$ and $\rho_{ICC}$. To each set, we applied the single-unit-per-stratum design. Then, we computed three approximations of the sampling variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator of the population mean: 1. The Horvitz-Thompson estimator for the sampling variance of the estimator for the population mean, $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$. 2. The bias-adjusted estimator, $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$. 3. The “collapsed stratum” estimator (Wolter, 2007, 51-2), which for this case, given unit $k$ from stratum 1 and unit $l$ from stratum 2 selected into $s^0$, equals, $$\widehat V_{CS}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = \frac{1}{N^2}\left(\frac{y_{k1}}{\pi_1} - \frac{y_{l2}}{\pi_2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}(y_{k1} - y_{l2})^2.$$” (The two misprints in these displays, the missing restriction to distinct units and $\epsilon_{is}$ for $\epsilon_{ks}$, are finding P027-E006; see P027-T18.) The supplement does not say that the errors $\epsilon_{ks}$ are independent, or that the two strata are sampled independently; both are the ordinary reading and are used by the validators.
[Supplement, Section C, systematic PPS sampling: pp. A3–A4 (supplement PDF pp. 3–4)] “For the simulations, a size variable, $x = (x_1, ..., x_N)$, is produced as a vector of $N$ random draws from a negative binomial distribution with mean 6, variance 16, and offset of 1 to avoid zero values. These settings were meant to recreate a data scenario roughly comparable to Wolter (2007, Ch. 8). An outcome variable, $y$, is created as, $$y_k = \beta x_k + \epsilon_k,$$ for $k = 1, ..., N$, where $\beta = \rho(\sigma_y/\sigma_x)$, $\epsilon_k$ is Gaussian noise with mean zero and standard deviation $\sigma_y\sqrt{1 - \rho^2}$, and $\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_y$ are the standard deviation of the $N$ values in $x$ and $y$ respectively, where $\mathrm{E}_x(\sigma_x) = 4$ and we fix $\sigma_y = 30$ (again, to mimic data distributed as in Wolter (2007, Ch. 8)). Thus, $x$ and $y$ have a linear relationship through the origin and their correlation is given by $\rho$. Systematic PPS sampling was implemented such that each unit's first order inclusion probability is given by, $$\pi_k = \frac{x_k}{\sum_{l=1}^{N} x_l}m,$$ where $m$ is the size of the systematic sample, and joint inclusion probabilities are computed as per Madow (1949).” The with-replacement estimator (p. A3): $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{WR}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = \frac{1}{N^2 m(m - 1)}\sum_{k \in s^0}\left(\frac{y_k}{p_k} - \hat t\right)^2,$$ “where $p_k = \pi_k/m$ is the notional “per-draw” selection probability.” The periodic design (pp. A3–A4): “we performed a second set of simulations where the size variable, $x$, was drawn as an $N$-length vector of repeating 2's and 10's, thus maintaining variance values that are comparable to the previous simulation. Also, so that we could provide an illustration of the performance of $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$, we produced $y_k$ values in the same manner as above, but then worked with the demeaned value, $$\tilde y_k \equiv y_k - \bar y,$$ as the variable with which $\hat\mu_{HT}$ was computed.” The supplement does not display the systematic selection rule; the validators and the targets below use the usual cumulative-size rule with one uniform random start (unit $k$ occupies the interval $[c_{k-1}, c_k)$ with $c_k = \sum_{a \le k} x_a$; with $I = \sum_l x_l/m$ and $u$ uniform on $[0, I)$ the sample is the set of units whose intervals contain $u, u + I, \ldots, u + (m-1)I$), and the order $x = (2, 10, 2, 10, \ldots)$. The $(N, m)$ pairs of Tables A2 and A3 (pp. A7–A8) are $(8, 2), (40, 2), (120, 30), (600, 30), (240, 60), (1200, 60)$, so $q = N/m \in \{4, 20\}$.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Supplement Section B, last paragraph: ‘The $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$ estimator dominates $\widehat V_{CS}(\hat\mu_{HT})$ for smaller stratum sizes and the two perform similarly for larger stratum sizes’; the witnesses are the validator's and are not in the paper
canonical_claim.location: Supplement p. A2 (staged/supplements/smj_suppl.pdf, PDF p. 2), Section B, last paragraph; Table A1 on supplement p. A5 (PDF p. 5)
canonical_claim.statement:
Exact witnesses (validator's constructions; not in the paper) that the comparison of the corrected estimator with the collapsed-stratum estimator depends on the stratum means as well as on the stratum size $M$, and that large strata alone do not make the two similar.
Setting: the one-unit-per-stratum design of supplement Section B (two strata of $M$ units, $N = 2M$, one unit drawn uniformly from each stratum, independently), with the three estimators $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$, $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$ and $\widehat V_{CS}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = \tfrac14(y_{k1} - y_{l2})^2$.
(C1) [Two fixed populations with the same stratum size.] $M = 5$; deviations $e = (3/2, -3/2, 1/2, -1/2, 0)$; stratum 1 has outcomes $\alpha + e_i$ and stratum 2 has outcomes $-\alpha + e_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, 5$; the 25 samples have probability $1/25$ each. For both $\alpha = 0$ and $\alpha = 2$, $\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = 1/2$. For $\alpha = 0$: $\mathrm{E}[(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)] = 2/5$, $\mathrm{E}[(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)] = 4/5$, $\mathrm{E}[\widehat V_{CS}] = 1/2$; the bias of the corrected estimator is $3/10$ and that of the collapsed-stratum estimator is $0$. For $\alpha = 2$: the three expectations are $2$, $4$ and $9/2$; the biases are $7/2$ and $4$. So at one and the same stratum size the bias ranking of the two estimators reverses with $\alpha$.
(C2) [The same under the outcome model.] With the model-averaged biases $B_{C2}$ and $B_{CS}$ of P027-T15 (iii): at $M = 5$, $\alpha = 0$: $B_{C2} = 2/5 > B_{CS} = 1/10$; at $M = 5$, $\alpha = 2$: $B_{C2} = 18/5 < B_{CS} = 41/10$.
(C3) [Large strata are not enough.] At $M = 500$, $\alpha = 0$ (model-averaged): the true variance is $499/1000$, the expected corrected estimate is $499/500$ and the expected collapsed-stratum estimate is $1/2$; the relative biases are $1$ and $1/499$.
For comparison, Table A1 as printed (supplement p. A5; columns $\rho_{ICC}$; $M$; True Var; Mean from sims. $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{HT}$, $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}$, $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{CS}$; Relative Bias; Nominal Bias), row 2: 0.00; 5; 0.39; 0.39, 0.79, 0.49; 0.00, 1.03, 0.26; 0.00, 0.40, 0.10. Row 5: 0.00; 500; 0.50; 0.50, 1.00, 0.50; 0.00, 1.00, 0.00; 0.00, 0.50, 0.00. Row 15: 0.50; 500; 0.50; 0.75, 1.50, 1.00; 0.50, 2.01, 1.01; 0.25, 1.00, 0.50.
What the witnesses contradict: the unqualified summary that the corrected estimator dominates the collapsed-stratum estimator for smaller stratum sizes and that the two perform similarly for larger stratum sizes, read as a statement about their biases as approximations to the true sampling variance.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The design, $\pi_{ks}$, $\pi_{ks,lt}$, the outcome model, $\rho_{ICC}$, the three estimators and $\widehat V_{CS}$: supplement pp. A1–A2, standing assumptions. $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ and $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$: main pp. 233 and 237. ‘dominates’ and ‘perform similarly’ are not defined; the paragraph compares the estimators ‘as an approximation to the true sampling variance’ through their expected values (Section A: ‘All simulations study expected values of estimators’), so the reading is by bias. In (C1) the populations are fixed and the expectations are over the 25 samples; in (C2) and (C3) they are also averaged over the outcome model.
canonical_claim.note: P027-E001 is rated an error, Minor. Sol's verdict is confirmed_in_part, evidence type exact_counterexample, upheld on re-run. Not refuted: the first clause for the smallest displayed size $M = 2$ (weak dominance, tie at $\alpha = 0$), the visual similarity of the high-correlation curves in Figure A1, and the main text's weaker claim (p. 240, ‘less biased ... in a range of scenarios’). No mean-squared-error statement is made. Numbers are from the validator's derivation.md, section 5, and check_output.txt, recomputed independently; the table rows were read from the rendered supplement page (PDF p. 5).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Supplement Section B, last paragraph, the comparison of $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$ with $\widehat V_{CS}(\hat\mu_{HT})$, corrected: the bias ranking by $M$ and $\alpha$
canonical_claim.location: Supplement p. A2 (staged/supplements/smj_suppl.pdf, PDF p. 2), Section B, last paragraph; the design and estimators on supplement pp. A1–A2
canonical_claim.statement:
Sol's repair (validated.json, P027-E001, smallest_repair), verbatim: "Replace the sentence by a parameter-qualified bias comparison: Averaging over the sampling design and generated populations, the corrected estimator has smaller bias than the collapsed-stratum estimator when M<2(1+alpha^2), with a tie at equality and the reverse ranking otherwise. For large M their expected estimates have ratio approximately 2-rho_ICC, so large strata alone do not imply similar approximation accuracy; the expected estimates are relatively close when rho_ICC is near 1."
Mathematical content, with every hypothesis (validator's derivation.md, sections 1–4 and 6).
Setting. Two strata $s = 1, 2$, each of $M \ge 2$ units; $N = 2M$. Design: one unit $K$ drawn uniformly from stratum 1 and one unit $L$ drawn uniformly from stratum 2, independently; so $\pi_{ks} = 1/M$, $\pi_{ks,lt} = 1/M^2$ for $s \ne t$ and $\pi_{ks,ls} = 0$ for $k \ne l$. For a fixed population $y = (y_{ks})$ write $x = y_{K1}$ and $z = y_{L2}$ for the two sampled outcomes.
(i) [The estimators, sample by sample, for any fixed population.] $\hat\mu_{HT} = (x + z)/2$; $$\frac{1}{N^2}\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t) = \frac{M - 1}{4M}(x^2 + z^2), \qquad \frac{1}{N^2}\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t) = \frac{M - 1}{2M}(x^2 + z^2) = 2\cdot\frac{1}{N^2}\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t), \qquad \widehat V_{CS}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = \frac14(x - z)^2.$$
(ii) [The true variance for a fixed population.] $\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu_{HT}) = (v_1 + v_2)/4$, where $v_s = \frac1M\sum_k y_{ks}^2 - \big(\frac1M\sum_k y_{ks}\big)^2$.
(iii) [Averages over the outcome model, second moments only.] Let $y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{ks}$ with $\alpha_1 = \alpha = -\alpha_2$ and errors $\epsilon_{ks}$ with mean zero, variance one and zero covariances (independent $\mathrm{N}(0,1)$ in the supplement). Write $\mathrm{E}$ for expectation over the errors and the sample. Then $$\mathrm{E}\big[\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu_{HT})\big] = \frac{M - 1}{2M}, \quad \mathrm{E}\Big[\frac{1}{N^2}\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)\Big] = \frac{M - 1}{2M}(1 + \alpha^2), \quad \mathrm{E}\Big[\frac{1}{N^2}\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)\Big] = \frac{M - 1}{M}(1 + \alpha^2), \quad \mathrm{E}\big[\widehat V_{CS}\big] = \alpha^2 + \frac12,$$ and the averaged biases are $$B_{HT} = \frac{M - 1}{2M}\alpha^2, \qquad B_{C2} = \frac{M - 1}{2M}(1 + 2\alpha^2), \qquad B_{CS} = \alpha^2 + \frac{1}{2M},$$ all nonnegative.
(iv) [The ranking.] $$B_{C2} - B_{CS} = \frac{M - 2 - 2\alpha^2}{2M} = \frac12 - \frac{1 + \alpha^2}{M}.$$ Hence $B_{C2} < B_{CS}$ if and only if $M < 2(1 + \alpha^2)$; $B_{C2} = B_{CS}$ if and only if $M = 2(1 + \alpha^2)$; and $B_{C2} > B_{CS}$ if and only if $M > 2(1 + \alpha^2)$. In terms of the printed $\rho_{ICC} = \alpha^2/(\alpha^2 + 1/2)$: $B_{C2} < B_{CS}$ if and only if $\rho_{ICC} > (M - 2)/(M - 1)$.
(v) [Large strata.] $$\frac{\mathrm{E}\big[(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)\big]}{\mathrm{E}\big[\widehat V_{CS}\big]} = \Big(1 - \frac1M\Big)\frac{1 + \alpha^2}{1/2 + \alpha^2} = \Big(1 - \frac1M\Big)(2 - \rho_{ICC}),$$ and the difference of the two expectations is $\tfrac12 - (1 + \alpha^2)/M$; as $M \to \infty$ with $\alpha$ fixed the ratio tends to $2 - \rho_{ICC}$ and the difference to $1/2$, the limit of the true variance. So large strata alone do not make the two estimates close; they are relatively close only when $\rho_{ICC}$ is near 1.
This is a statement about biases averaged over the design and the generated populations; it is not a mean-squared-error ranking.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The design, $\pi_{ks}$, $\pi_{ks,lt}$ (with the restriction to distinct units restored: P027-T18), the outcome model $y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{ks}$, $\alpha_1 = \alpha = -\alpha_2$, $\rho_{ICC}$, and $\widehat V_{CS}(\hat\mu_{HT})$: supplement pp. A1–A2, standing assumptions. $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$: main p. 233; $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_{C2}(\hat t)$: main p. 237 (P027-T23); $\hat\mu_{HT} \equiv \hat t/N$: supplement p. A1. Bias of an estimator $W$: $\mathrm{E}[W] - \mathrm{E}[\mathrm{Var}(\hat\mu_{HT})]$, the expectation of the conditional design bias (the ‘True Var’ column of Table A1 is on the scale $(M-1)/(2M)$: 0.25, 0.40, 0.475, 0.495, 0.499). Independence of the two strata's draws and of the errors is the ordinary reading; (iii) needs only uncorrelated unit-variance errors.
canonical_claim.note: Repair cost recorded by Sol: weaker_conclusion (the comparison is qualified by both stratum size and between-stratum means; no assumption, estimand or estimator changes). The limits named in (v) follow at once from the exact formulas for each $M$. The supplement's other sentence, that $(1/N^2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat t)$ strictly dominates both alternatives, is consistent with (iii): $B_{HT} \le B_{C2}$ and $B_{HT} < B_{CS}$ for every $M$ and $\alpha$; it was checked by the readers and is not a finding.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Supplement Section B: ‘the intra-class correlation over strata is given by, $\rho_{ICC} = \frac{\alpha^2}{\alpha^2 + 1/2}$’; the witness is the validator's and is not in the paper
canonical_claim.location: Supplement p. A2 (staged/supplements/smj_suppl.pdf, PDF p. 2), Section B, first lines of the page; the labels of Table A1 (supplement p. A5) and Figure A1 (supplement p. A6) use the parameter
canonical_claim.statement:
Exact witness (validator's construction; not in the paper): a value of $\alpha$ at which the printed ratio differs from the correlation of two distinct units of the same stratum in the stated model.
Model. $S$ takes the values $+1$ and $-1$ with probability $1/2$ each (the stratum of the pair, the two strata being of equal size); $\epsilon$ and $\epsilon'$ have mean zero and variance one; $S$, $\epsilon$, $\epsilon'$ are independent (uncorrelatedness of $\epsilon$ and $\epsilon'$ and $\mathrm{E}[S\epsilon] = \mathrm{E}[S\epsilon'] = 0$ are all that is used); $Y = \alpha S + \epsilon$ and $Y' = \alpha S + \epsilon'$ are the outcomes of two distinct units of the same stratum, with stratum means $\alpha_1 = \alpha = -\alpha_2$.
Witness: $\alpha = 1/2$.
(C1) $\mathrm{E}(Y) = \mathrm{E}(Y') = 0$, $\mathrm{Var}(Y) = \mathrm{Var}(Y') = 5/4$, $\mathrm{Cov}(Y, Y') = 1/4$, so $\mathrm{Corr}(Y, Y') = 1/5$.
(C2) The printed formula gives $\rho_{ICC} = \frac{1/4}{1/4 + 1/2} = 1/3 \ne 1/5$; the difference is $2/15$.
(C3) The printed value is the ratio $S_\alpha^2/(S_\alpha^2 + 1)$ with $S_\alpha^2 = \big[(\alpha - 0)^2 + (-\alpha - 0)^2\big]/(2 - 1) = 1/2$, the divisor-1 variance of the two fixed stratum means; their divisor-2 variance is $1/4 = \mathrm{Var}(\alpha S)$.
What the witness contradicts: the description of $\alpha^2/(\alpha^2 + 1/2)$ as the intra-class correlation, read as the ordinary correlation of two units of the same stratum.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The model $y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{ks}$, $\epsilon_{ks} \sim \mathrm{N}(0,1)$, $\alpha_1 = \alpha = -\alpha_2$, two strata each of size $M$, and the display for $\rho_{ICC}$: supplement pp. A1–A2, standing assumptions. ‘Intra-class correlation over strata’ is not defined in the supplement; the reading tested is the Pearson correlation of the outcomes of two distinct units that share a stratum, the stratum being equally likely to be either (the strata have equal sizes). Conditional on a given stratum the correlation is zero.
canonical_claim.note: P027-A001 is rated an error, Minor. Sol's verdict is confirmed_in_part, evidence type exact_counterexample, upheld on re-run. Not established: any arithmetic error in the printed ratio as a variance-ratio (Bessel or ANOVA) parameter, or any effect on estimator values or on comparisons within a scenario; which convention the authors intended cannot be inferred from the page.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Supplement Section B, the display for $\rho_{ICC}$, corrected: the printed ratio is a variance-ratio parameter with the divisor-1 variance of the two stratum means; the same-stratum pair correlation is $\alpha^2/(\alpha^2 + 1)$
canonical_claim.location: Supplement p. A2 (staged/supplements/smj_suppl.pdf, PDF p. 2), Section B, first lines of the page; Table A1 (supplement p. A5) and Figure A1 (supplement p. A6)
canonical_claim.statement:
Sol's repair (validated.json, P027-A001, smallest_repair), verbatim: "Define the displayed quantity as a fixed-stratum simulation heterogeneity parameter q=S_alpha^2/(S_alpha^2+1)=alpha^2/(alpha^2+1/2), with S_alpha^2=sum_s(alpha_s-alpha_bar)^2/(2-1)=2alpha^2. Use q in the A2 description, Table A1, and Figure A1, and state separately that the ordinary same-stratum population pair correlation is r=alpha^2/(alpha^2+1)=q/(2-q). This preserves all printed simulation parameter values. Alternatively, retain the ordinary correlation label, change 1/2 to 1 in the formula, and convert the table/figure coordinates by r=p/(2-p) without changing the underlying scenarios."
Mathematical content, with every hypothesis (validator's derivation.md, sections 2, 4 and 6).
Setting. $\alpha$ real. $S \in \{+1, -1\}$ with probability $1/2$ each; $\epsilon, \epsilon'$ with mean zero and variance one; $\mathrm{E}[S\epsilon] = \mathrm{E}[S\epsilon'] = \mathrm{E}[\epsilon\epsilon'] = 0$ (in the supplement the errors are $\mathrm{N}(0,1)$, read as independent); $Y = \alpha S + \epsilon$, $Y' = \alpha S + \epsilon'$.
(i) [The pair correlation.] $\mathrm{Var}(Y) = \mathrm{Var}(Y') = \alpha^2 + 1$, $\mathrm{Cov}(Y, Y') = \alpha^2$, and $$r := \mathrm{Corr}(Y, Y') = \frac{\alpha^2}{\alpha^2 + 1}.$$
(ii) [What the printed ratio is.] With $\bar\alpha = (\alpha_1 + \alpha_2)/2 = 0$ and $S_\alpha^2 = \sum_{s=1}^{2}(\alpha_s - \bar\alpha)^2/(2 - 1) = 2\alpha^2$, $$q := \frac{S_\alpha^2}{S_\alpha^2 + 1} = \frac{2\alpha^2}{2\alpha^2 + 1} = \frac{\alpha^2}{\alpha^2 + 1/2},$$ the printed $\rho_{ICC}$.
(iii) [They differ unless $\alpha = 0$.] $$q - r = \frac{\alpha^2}{(\alpha^2 + 1)(2\alpha^2 + 1)} \ge 0,$$ with equality if and only if $\alpha = 0$.
(iv) [Conversion.] For $0 \le q < 1$: $\alpha^2 = \frac{q}{2(1 - q)}$ and $r = \frac{q}{2 - q}$; the map $q \mapsto q/(2 - q)$ is strictly increasing on $[0, 1)$ with limit $1$ at $1$. (So the printed labels $0.33, 0.50, 0.67, 0.82, 0.90, 0.99$, taken as exact, correspond to pair correlations $33/167$, $1/3$, $67/133$, $41/59$, $9/11$, $99/101$.)
Corrected text: the displayed quantity is a simulation heterogeneity parameter $q$; Table A1 and Figure A1 are indexed by $q$; the same-stratum pair correlation under independent outcome errors is $r = q/(2 - q)$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The model, the two strata, $\alpha_1 = \alpha = -\alpha_2$ and the display for $\rho_{ICC}$: supplement pp. A1–A2, standing assumptions. $S$ is the stratum of the pair, uniform on the two strata because they have the same size $M$; $Y, Y'$ are two distinct units of that stratum, which exist for $M \ge 2$. The symbol $q$ here is Sol's name for the printed ratio (it is not the $q = N/m$ of the systematic-sampling targets).
canonical_claim.note: Repair cost recorded by Sol: none (a definition and labelling clarification; the relabelling is monotone, so the scenario ordering, all estimator values and all comparisons within a scenario are unchanged). The validator also shows that the printed ratio equals an ANOVA ratio of expected mean squares, $(\mathrm{E}[MS_B] - \mathrm{E}[MS_W])/(\mathrm{E}[MS_B] + (M-1)\mathrm{E}[MS_W])$ with $\mathrm{E}[MS_B] = 2M\alpha^2 + 1$ and $\mathrm{E}[MS_W] = 1$ (derivation.md, section 5); that route is not part of this target.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Supplement Section B, the display for the joint inclusion probabilities $\pi_{ks,lt}$ (the restriction to distinct units is missing) and the display $y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{is}$ (index $i$ for $k$), corrected
canonical_claim.location: Supplement p. A1 (staged/supplements/smj_suppl.pdf, PDF p. 1), Section B, the last two displays of the page; continued on supplement p. A2 (PDF p. 2); the convention $\pi_{kk} = \pi_k$ is on main p. 233 (PDF p. 5)
canonical_claim.statement:
Sol's repair (validated.json, P027-E006, smallest_repair), parts (c) and (d), verbatim: "(c) Prefix the joint-inclusion display with “For distinct units $(k,s)\ne(l,t)$”; keep its cases, and, if desired, state $\pi_{ks,ks}=1/M$. (d) $y_{ks}=\alpha_s+\epsilon_{ks}$."
As printed (supplement p. A1): “and for units $k$ and $l$ in strata 1 or 2, we have $$\pi_{ks,lt} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } s = t \\ \frac{1}{M^2} & \text{if } s \neq t \end{cases}.$$ In stratum $s$, outcomes $y_s = (y_{1s}, ..., y_{Ms})$ are drawn as, $$y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{is},$$” [p. A2] “where $\alpha_s$ is a stratum-specific constant and $\epsilon_{ks} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, 1)$.”
Mathematical content of (c), with every hypothesis. Setting: two strata $s = 1, 2$, each of $M \ge 1$ units, unit $k$ of stratum $s$ written $(k, s)$; one unit is drawn uniformly at random from each stratum, the two draws being independent; $I_{ks}$ is the inclusion indicator of $(k, s)$ and $\pi_{ks,lt} = \mathrm{E}(I_{ks}I_{lt})$.
(i) $\pi_{ks} = \mathrm{E}(I_{ks}) = 1/M$ for every unit.
(ii) For distinct units $(k, s) \ne (l, t)$: $$\pi_{ks,lt} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } s = t \\ \frac{1}{M^2} & \text{if } s \neq t. \end{cases}$$
(iii) On the diagonal, $\pi_{ks,ks} = \pi_{ks} = 1/M$ (since $I_{ks}^2 = I_{ks}$; main p. 233: ‘$\mathrm{E}(I_k I_k) = \pi_{kk} = \pi_k$ by construction’). So the printed display, which assigns $0$ whenever $s = t$ without excluding $(k, s) = (l, t)$, is wrong on the diagonal: for $M = 2$ it gives $0$ where the value is $1/2$.
(iv) Consequently $\mathrm{Cov}(I_{ks}, I_{lt}) = 0$ for $s \ne t$, $\mathrm{Cov}(I_{ks}, I_{ls}) = -1/M^2$ for $k \ne l$, and $\mathrm{Var}(I_{ks}) = \frac1M\big(1 - \frac1M\big)$.
Content of (d): the outcome model of Section B is $y_{ks} = \alpha_s + \epsilon_{ks}$ for unit $k$ of stratum $s$, with $\alpha_s$ a stratum-specific constant and $\epsilon_{ks} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, 1)$; the index $i$ of the printed display is not introduced anywhere and stands for $k$. This is a definition (it is the model used in P027-T14 to P027-T17) and carries no claim to prove.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: $I_k$, $\pi_k$, $\pi_{kl}$, $\pi_{kk} = \pi_k$, $\mathrm{Cov}(I_k, I_l) = \pi_{kl} - \pi_k\pi_l$: main p. 233 (PDF p. 5), standing assumptions. ‘two strata each of size $M$, in which case $N = 2M$. From each stratum a single unit is randomly sampled’: supplement p. A1. The supplement does not say that the two strata are sampled independently; the printed value $1/M^2$ for $s \ne t$ presupposes it.
canonical_claim.note: P027-E006 is rated an error, Minor: four misprints, each corrected on sight. Parts (c) and (d) are misprints inside a formula and are covered here. Parts (a) (the proof of Corollary 2 ends ‘Proposition 1 therefore holds’ where Proposition 2 is applied; noted at P027-T23) and (b) (‘remains’ for ‘remain’, main p. 231) are a cross-reference and a grammatical slip and are not targets. Sol's verdict is confirmed (batch validation, complete derivation; work/check_calculations.py records the $M = 2$ diagonal value). No result changes.
